quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left, what does it mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals to show turns and stops when they do not have turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or move into the left lane.

questions.question: What can help fix a drive chain that is slipping?
questions.explanation: If the chain slips, try tightening it. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, how should you adjust for the extra weight?

options.text: Keep a shorter distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Brake later than you normally would.

questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what rule applies?

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if you started before it began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the posted speed limit and only happen in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, should you use both brakes?

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: By changing power suddenly in a turn.
While riding the brake through a turn.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road are all more hazardous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Both your eyes and your face.
Your face but not your eyes.
Your eyes but not your face.
Neither your eyes nor your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield can protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will appear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear while going too fast can cause your motorcycle to jerk and the rear tire to skid, making you lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for one rider to finish passing before the next rider starts.
Have several riders pass the vehicle at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no more motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for one rider to finish passing before the next rider starts.
questions.explanation: In a group, riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing and return to formation before the next rider passes.

questions.question: In a normal turn, what should happen?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays straight.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid hazards, escape danger, and communicate with other drivers. It does not help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a replacement for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position yourself in the lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to stay away from oncoming traffic.
Weave slightly in your lane to make your headlight more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself in the lane where other drivers will see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: Move into the part of your lane that makes you visible to oncoming drivers as soon as possible. For example, if turning right, move to the left side of your lane so drivers can see you sooner.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: May help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: May help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A bright helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers notice you.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Drivers must follow these rules.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take before a rider feels the effects?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handle grips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip both handle grips firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What operates the gearshift lever?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle sits lower and weighs more. Ride a bit slower than usual, especially in curves and over bumps. The extra weight means your bike takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep more distance between your bike and other vehicles.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see better, avoid hazards, escape from danger, and stay out of blind spots. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.
